What was removed, and why?

CAMERA SUPPORT CHECKED BEFORE ANY DELETION

Frame 230 was supported by only six surviving sparse-point observations and was positioned far outside the other recovered cameras. The original trainer estimated scene size from the maximum camera radius. This one pose inflated its scene scale from roughly 2.48 to 21.65, increasing Gaussian position learning rates and size thresholds.

The cleanup excludes cameras with fewer than 20 surviving 3D-point observations or a radius above five times the median. Support is measured before deletion to avoid a cascade. COLMAP removes their observations and points that lose sufficient track support. No bundle adjustment or new camera calibration is performed in this trial.

Excluded framePoint observationsReason

Six frames are excluded from Gaussian training: 227, 228, 229, 230, 232 and 243. The copy retains 487 recovered views, 425 training images and all 62 original validation images. Only 31 sparse points are removed. The original capture still contains all 500 source frames.

Reproducible settings

ONE CONTROLLED INPUT CLEANUP
  1. Copy the original full-resolution undistorted COLMAP model and apply the documented camera-support filter.
  2. Validate that the retained cameras, intrinsics and photograph dimensions agree with the first attempt; preserve the original validation split.
  3. Train official gsplat 1.5.3 for 30,000 steps on the RTX 4090, using data factor 1, packed rasterization, batch size 1, SH degree 3 and seed 42.
  4. Use the original default growth and pruning strategy: refinement every 100 steps from after step 500 until step 15,000; gradient threshold 0.0002; split-scale threshold 0.01 × scene scale; pruning threshold 0.1 × scene scale; opacity threshold 0.005. Pose and appearance optimization remain disabled.
  5. Evaluate and save checkpoints at 7,000 and 30,000 steps. Compare the same 62 held-out views, inspect prediction images and validate the exported PLY.

This tests camera and sparse-track cleanup together. A better result would support the diagnosis, but it would not isolate the effect of frame 230 alone or establish measured room accuracy. Remaining blur, reflections, video artifacts and poorly observed surfaces may still limit quality.
